summary.headline: Borosil FY26 revenue rose 8% to INR1,195.9 crore but operating EBITDA was flat at INR176.7 crore as Hydra flask supply disruption from the BIS QCO hit margins.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached INR1,195.9 crore (up 8% from INR1,107.8 crore), while pre-exceptional operating EBITDA was flat at INR176.7 crore and margin fell to 15.1% from 16.3%. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 5.2% to INR284.1 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% from 14.2%, with the West Asia LPG supply disruption temporarily shutting the borosilicate and opal glass furnaces. Management attributed the Hydra shortfall to BIS/QCO-related supply chain problems and said the company is adding in-house flask capacity and solar power to offset cost pressures. Net debt at consolidated level was INR49.7 crore at FY26 end.

segments.name: Larah opalware
segments.commentary: Sales INR411.9 crore in FY26 vs INR383.8 crore in FY25, +7.3%. Utilisation is 90-95% and the category has slowed.

segments.name: Glassware (borosilicate pressware, microwavable, tumblers, lunchboxes)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR295.5 crore in FY26 vs INR252 crore, +17.3%. Roughly two-thirds is made in-house, the rest is outsourced.

segments.name: Non-glassware (appliances, insulated bottles/flasks, cookware)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR463.7 crore in FY26 vs INR452.9 crore, +2.4%. Hydra flask sales were hit hard by non-availability under the BIS/QCO regime.

guidance_outlook: Management targets revenue growth of 15-20% YoY and EBITDA margin near 20% in the medium term.
Solar 20 MW plant with BESS (INR75 crore capex) to be commissioned in Q1 FY27; expected FY27 EBITDA benefit about INR28 crore, with solar taking care of about 61% of power needs after phase III.

Hydra flask in-house manufacturing (INR65 crore, subsidiary Stylenest India): first 2 lines to start commercial production before end-Q1 FY27, third line by end-Q2 FY27. Gross margin uplift of at least 10% expected, but realised only after 6-12 months of stabilisation.
Opalware: muted growth expected for the next year or so; no major opalware capex, debottlenecking only.

Glassware: Bharuch capacity for bottles, jugs and jars (INR42 crore, via outsourced vendor) expected by end-Q3 FY27. Pressware furnace expansion from 25 to 32 tonnes per day (INR50 crore) likely in FY27 or FY28.
Price hikes of 8-10% taken; management believes they are enough to cover cost inflation, but pass-through lags by 1-2 quarters.
FY27 capex about INR110 crore, plus maintenance capex of INR20-25 crore a year. More non-glassware capex under discussion, not yet Board-approved.
Direct incremental gas cost of about INR30-35 crore per annum due to the West Asia crisis, which management said is changing weekly.
BIS/QCO remediation deadline extended to 1 October 2026; appliance inventory built up to cover it.
capex_capacity: Hydra flask plant (Stylenest India): INR65 crore, 3 double-wall lines; first 2 lines in Q1 FY27, third by end-Q2 FY27.
Solar 20 MW ground-mounted plant with battery storage: INR75 crore, commissioning Q1 FY27.
Pressware furnace expansion 25 to 32 tonnes per day with a third forming line: about INR50 crore, FY27 or FY28 depending on furnace life.
Bharuch glassware (bottles, jugs, jars) via Borosil Scientific: about INR42 crore, by end-Q3 FY27.
Current capacity: opalware furnaces of 84 tonnes per day, borosilicate glassware plant of 25 tonnes per day. Opalware utilisation 90-95%, glassware running close to 90%.
demand_pricing: Hydra flask volumes were hit by product non-availability from the BIS/QCO implementation; management estimated about INR100 crore of Hydra loss in FY26 (per a prior interview), with losses in H1 and more in H2.
Chinese dumping of borosilicate and other glass is pressuring margins. An anti-dumping application covers only borosilicate glass; the decision is expected in 6-9 months.

Gas cost rose sharply from the West Asia crisis. Q4 FY26 furnaces at Jaipur and the borosilicate pressware site were shut for LPG-related supply restrictions; management said the shutdown did not cut sales because of inventory, but it did hit fixed-cost absorption.
Opalware competition: management disputed dealer reports of aggressive pricing and said pressure is on costs, not price.
Advertising and sales promotion rose marginally to about INR88 crore from INR87 crore; power and fuel fell to INR78 crore from INR82.4 crore.
Shared service support income (other operating income) rose to INR26 crore from INR18.4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins fall in Q4 despite borosilicate ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Chinese dumping, which Borosil can only partly offset with brand premium, plus higher gas and raw material costs in Q4. A price increase was taken but its impact lags.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA saving from solar?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Anand Sultania estimated about INR28 crore at EBITDA level for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the opalware outlook and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 90-95%. Growth has slowed, and only debottlenecking is planned. No major opalware capex; focus is on other categories.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost inflation is covered by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price hikes of 8-10% are enough to cover cost inflation, with 1-2 quarters of lag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the incremental gas cost and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gas cost rose by about INR30 crore for all three furnaces. Management put the direct impact at INR30-35 crore a year, with indirect effects via packaging, freight and wages.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital and inventory rise, and when will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Hydra inventory from last year is largely depleted, but appliance inventory was built for QCO and borosilicate furnace output exceeds sales. Management expects inventory to stop growing this year and reverse next year.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin gain from in-house vacuum bottle manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 10% gross margin improvement, but only after 6-12 months of stabilisation, so not in the first couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund rising debt and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt may rise short term by about INR100 crore, but it expects FY27 capex to be similar to operating cash flow of about INR120 crore, so funding is internal.

risks_watch: Gas and LPG cost volatility from the West Asia crisis: direct cost increase of INR30-35 crore a year, plus indirect effects; Q4 furnace shutdowns.
Chinese dumping in borosilicate and glassware; anti-dumping outcome expected in 6-9 months and not yet certain.
Hydra flask recovery depends on the in-house plant ramp-up; margin benefit is delayed 6-12 months.
QCO/BIS remediation deadline 1 October 2026 for appliances; inventory build-up exposes working capital.
Opalware growth has slowed and management expects muted growth for about a year without new product innovation.
Rising debt (about INR100 crore added in the last two quarters, per an analyst) and ROCE pressure from inventory.
Related-party arrangement with Borosil Scientific (cost plus about 5%); management said it is less than 10% of Borosil sales and consolidation is uneconomic for now.
summary.management_tone: Candid and somewhat defensive on the year: management openly attributed the flat EBITDA and Q4 margin fall to Hydra supply problems, China dumping and gas costs, while stressing that these are short-term issues. Confident on long-term targets and new capacity, but evasive on the exact Hydra loss and specific margin guidance for FY27.
key_quotes: Borosil has delivered a reasonable performance in FY26 with revenue from operations reaching INR1,195.9 crores, up from INR1,107.8 crores during the last year.

We are now starting a new facility for vacuum-insulated stainless steel bottles, flasks and containers, and also expansion of our injection molding operations for the plastic lids that go on our lunchboxes.

So we are, as a team, fully committed to enhancing the revenue by 15% to 20% year-on-year, and achieving EBITDA of closer to 20-odd percent in the medium term, and we continue to work on that journey.

We do have reasonable amounts of inventory. So if the market supports we can grow even without having grown the -- without growing the production for at least 1.5 years or 2 because of the inventories that we are carrying today.

growth.why: Management targets 15-20% medium-term revenue growth and ~20% EBITDA margin, backed by specific capacity (Hydra flask lines by Q2 FY27, Bharuch glassware by Q3 FY27, furnace expansion FY27/FY28) but opalware growth is guided muted and the medium-term target lacks a dated build-up, so growth outlook is flat over the next four quarters.
